title: Atomic Creditline Breakdown & Export — Cost UX experiment
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Problem: Customers need a compact, auditable view of per-message and per-token charges that can be sliced by model, route, team, and prompt variant. Existing console panels show aggregate spend but lack an exportable, columnized ledger for downstream chargeback and compliance workflows. This ticket designs a new 'Atomic Creditline' panel: a token-aware ledger with inline attribution, column toggles, and CSV/JSONL export tailored to finance and SRE workflows.

Scope: design of UI patterns (table, pivot controls, attribution ribbons), export formats and schema, lightweight on-screen summarization (sparkline + median cost), and privacy-aware defaults (masking PII in exports). Not in scope: backend billing ingestion pipeline, but includes acceptance criteria for sample export payloads for engineering to validate integration.
acceptance_criteria: High-fidelity Figma prototype for Atomic Creditline panel with table, column chooser, and attribution ribbon
Export implemented spec: CSV (flat rows) and JSONL (line-level metadata) examples attached and validated by ENG
UI supports filters by date range, model, route, team, and prompt-tag; results match sample dataset in Confluence PRD
Performance guardrails: table loads first 200 rows quickly; full exports run as background job with progress indicator
Accessibility: table keyboard nav + screen-reader labels verified by design QA
Edge cases documented: suppressed tokens, anonymized prompt content, and rate-limited export retries
comments: 2025-01-18 Asha: Kickoff — captured PM ask (detailed per-token attribution for chargeback + forensic export). Initial sketches attached.
2025-01-24 Maya: Low-fi usability session with 3 finance reps; main feedback: need consistent column names and a canonical 'billing id' per invocation for reconciliation.

2025-01-30 Eng (Luca): Feasibility note — computing full token-level attribution in real-time is expensive. Proposal: show lightweight on-screen attribution (sampled or rolled up) and trigger background export job that materializes per-token rows offline.
2025-02-05 PM (Riley): Agreed on background export pattern; requested progress indicator and webhook callback when export is ready.
2025-02-12 Design review: move column chooser into collapsible side rail; add a compact density mode for customers who need thousands of rows onscreen.
2025-02-17 Accessibility review: ensure CSV export includes header rows with human-readable labels and locale-aware number formatting options.
2025-02-20 Asha: Prototype updated with JSONL schema sample; flagged two engineering follow-ups (ENG-98521 for export job API, ENG-98522 for anonymization toggle).
tradeoffs_and_decisions: Decision: Use background export job for full per-token dumps to avoid impacting interactive console latency. Rationale: protects SLOs for console and serving runtime.
Trade-off: On-screen attribution will be approximate (rolled-up by token class) for speed vs. full fidelity in exports. Documented on PRD so customers understand differences.
Decision: Offer CSV and JSONL exports. CSV for finance teams (flat rows), JSONL for engineers and forensic tooling (nested metadata in single-line JSON objects per event).
Trade-off: Include a hashed prompt_id in exports by default; full prompt text requires Opt-in export with consent and masking options. Balances auditability with privacy/regulatory needs.
open_questions: Should we expose per-token GPU-cost attribution or stick to amortized per-token USD cost? (Pending pricing team input)
What retention window do customers expect for exported CSVs via console? (Default 30 days vs enterprise retention policy)
Webhook API contract for export completion — which fields should be included to allow automated ingestion by customer systems?
next_steps: Finalize JSONL/CSV export schema and attach canonical example payloads to PRD (owner: Maya)
ENG to implement background export job and webhook (owner: Luca, linked ENG-98521)
Schedule 1-hour design + PM + Eng sync to agree on anonymization toggle and default masking rules (by 2025-02-28)
Run 2 moderated usability sessions with finance and platform teams on the Figma prototype (recruit via solutions-eng)
Add telemetry spec for export events (who requested, size, duration) for future cost optimization analysis
notes: Prototype intentionally emphasizes discoverability of the export and column semantics over dense visualization. The design pattern here is a ledger-first UX with an attribution ribbon that surfaces primary drivers (model, tokens, system prompt) and a secondary details pane for the export schema. Plan to iterate after initial customer trials.
implementation_considerations: Engineering must avoid synchronous tokenization and cost aggregation in the UI request path. Recommend backend endpoint /exports/creditline with async job semantics, incremental progress, and a signed download URL returned via webhook. Export rows should include stable identifiers: billing_id, invocation_id, model_id, route, timestamp, token_count, token_cost_usd, attribution_tags.
